archetypes.name: cross-doc-drift
archetypes.rationale: The rename gate is referenced across design prose, skill steps, and admit-check docs; any file not in scope-files.txt that still describes the old PUBLISH_OK-gated order becomes a stale contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read every file in scope-files.txt that documents the [DESIGNED] rename order or PUBLISH_OK admission gate, then grep for other files in the repo that reference the same gate (e.g. `PUBLISH_OK`, `[DESIGNED]`, `--state designed`, `tracking-issue-write.sh`) and are NOT listed in scope-files.txt. For each unlisted file, determine whether its prose or logic would conflict with the new post-diagram-upsert ordering after the plan lands. Flag any undeclared file whose description of the rename timing or admission criterion will be wrong after the change — these are missing scope entries, not minor nits. Also check whether `scripts/relevant-checks.sh` or the Makefile registers the new `test-design-log-publish.sh --scrub-only` harness; if not, flag the gap. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: arg-threading
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a new design-log-publish.sh --scrub-only call from design-publish.sh but does not verify that all required positional/flag arguments (--design-tmpdir, --run-id, --issue, --repo) are guaranteed to be set at that call site.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/scripts/design-publish.sh` and `scripts/design-log-publish.sh` and check whether every argument the plan threads to the `--scrub-only` call (`--design-tmpdir`, `--run-id`, `--issue`, `${REPO:+--repo "$REPO"}`) is guaranteed non-empty at that call site under all `SESSION_ID`-non-empty paths — including cases where an earlier step failed. Verify that `design-log-publish.sh` actually parses `--scrub-only` in its argument loop and that no existing `set -e` or `errexit` block could cause the scrub-only call to abort `design-publish.sh` before the final-summary render. Check whether `--scrub-only` reuses or skips any global variable assignments that the subsequent full-flush call also relies on, and whether calling `--scrub-only` first and then the full flush in the same shell process could cause variable collision or stale state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: result-env-chain
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds five new result keys (SCRUB_OK, ADMISSION_READY, ADMISSION_BLOCK_REASON, RENAME_FAILED, RENAME_NOOP) that must be written by write_result_env_and_emit, parsed by the SKILL.md Step 5c block, and consumed by Step 5d footer logic — any break in that three-step chain silently drops the new state.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/SKILL.md` Step 5c parser block and `skills/design/scripts/design-publish.sh` result-env write section; check that every new key the plan adds (`SCRUB_OK`, `ADMISSION_READY`, `ADMISSION_BLOCK_REASON`, `RENAME_FAILED`, `RENAME_NOOP`) appears in (a) the `write_result_env_and_emit` call or equivalent persist step, (b) the SKILL.md Step 5c initialization+parse block for both result-env-file and stdout-fallback paths, and (c) the Step 5d / footer conditional logic that branches on `ADMISSION_READY` vs `ADMISSION_BLOCK_REASON`. Flag any key that is written but not parsed, parsed but not acted on, or whose fallback path is missing. Also check whether `render-final-summary.sh` reads these from the exported env vars (`DESIGN_PUBLISH_*`) rather than from the result-env file on disk, and whether the plan's export list matches what the script actually exports. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
